derived_from: T01 public comparables and existing Table design brief

hypotheses.possible_buyer: Employer or adviser with a specific payroll investment/change decision
hypotheses.proposition: A bounded decision pack using original cases, alternatives, evidence requirements and a practical briefing, with explicit internal-use rights.
hypotheses.test: Ask about a recent actual decision, what supported it, what remained unresolved, who owned the budget and what output could have changed the next action. Compare against the buyer’s actual free/internal alternatives.
hypotheses.counter_signal: Only general curiosity; free material already sufficient; no decision owner/use; requested evidence cannot be collected or responsibly generalised.
hypotheses.not_established: Willingness to pay, price, enterprise licence demand, repeat purchase or measured decision benefit.

hypotheses.possible_buyer: Relevant payroll ecosystem organisation funding defined independent work
hypotheses.proposition: Disclosed support for a research edition with specific aggregate outputs, recognition and separately defined reuse permissions.
hypotheses.test: Establish actual intended use, acceptable evidence and audience, approval/budget route, required rights and editorial expectations. Clarify whether the organisation actually wants research or meetings/contacts.
hypotheses.counter_signal: Value depends on default participant identities, guaranteed meetings, favourable findings, veto powers or unachievable exclusivity.
hypotheses.not_established: A sponsor commitment, launch funding, acceptable price, editorial independence contract or permission for commercial contact.

hypotheses.possible_buyer: No practitioner fee is proposed in the original Table concept; the participant contributes time and knowledge.
hypotheses.proposition: Relevant senior peers, useful findings and a practical follow-through benefit, with clear confidentiality and optional recognition.
hypotheses.test: Ask which peer/research output would earn their time, what they can appropriately share, existing alternatives, travel/employer constraints and preference for remote/written contribution. Keep research participation separate from future council interest.
hypotheses.counter_signal: Hospitality is the sole attraction; employer rules prevent attendance/sharing; peers or topics are irrelevant; little reason to return.
hypotheses.not_established: Accepted membership, actual eligible contribution, permission to publish, a continuing engagement pattern or a representative panel.

hypotheses.possible_buyer: JGA as programme owner and any separately identified funder
hypotheses.proposition: A small facilitated UK gathering might add case depth or peer value beyond the same research collected remotely.
hypotheses.test: Compare the same intended output with remote/written alternatives, identify what the room uniquely enables and what evidence would show it. Cost all staff, recruitment, hosting, travel and funding timing later.
hypotheses.counter_signal: Travel/hospitality add burden without distinct evidence or member value; uncertain funding precedes non-refundable costs; no responsible delivery owner.
hypotheses.not_established: Event preference, paid partner return, a venue budget, go/no-go thresholds or four-city viability.

validation_scope: Up to four exploratory Table contribution events, ideally two buyers and two prospective members; selective overlap only with actual eligible permissioned report input. Not a statistical market or pricing study.
